summary:
Farmer Helper is a Texas-focused agricultural analysis platform that brings farm location data, climate information, soil characteristics, crop history, and satellite-derived environmental layers together in one place. Its interactive map and farm data tools help users explore local conditions, compare crop rotations, and understand environmental trends that may inform planting decisions. The platform utilizes sources such as NASA POWER, MODIS, ECOSTRESS, SMAP, GPM, GRACE, FAO GAEZ, and USDA datasets, and makes complex geographic information easier to access and interpret.

Farmers often need to consult multiple sources to understand the conditions affecting a field. Farmer Helper addresses that challenge by organizing varied data in a unified, location-based experience, helping users identify relevant patterns without requiring specialist GIS tools. This is significant because clearer access to local climate, soil, and crop information can support more informed planning and strengthen resilience to changing environmental conditions. Although the application provides substantial information regarding local environmental information, it is intended as a tool for farmer judgement, and should not replace local expertise.
details:
Farmer Helper is an agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers better understand their land and make more informed decisions. Agricultural information is often spread across different websites, databases, and government resources, making it difficult to get a complete picture of a farm's conditions. Farmer Helper brings this information together in one place, allowing users to select a location and explore its soil characteristics, climate, weather, historical crop information, and satellite observations. Through an interactive 3D map and centralized dashboard, users can see how different environmental factors affect their land and explore potential crop-rotation strategies.

The platform collects information from several public data sources, including NASA POWER for climate data, USDA NRCS SSURGO for soil information, USDA NASS for historical crop coverage, and the National Weather Service for weather forecasts and alerts. It also incorporates NASA satellite observations and future climate projections through the Open-Meteo Climate API. By bringing these sources together, Farmer Helper gives users a more complete understanding of the conditions surrounding a selected farm. Users can also explore satellite and environmental raster layers, look through historical data, animate changes over time, and generate summaries for specific areas on the map.

One of the main features of Farmer Helper is its crop-rotation comparison system. It looks at available soil information, climate conditions, crop requirements, and user priorities to generate and compare different crop-rotation options. Instead of simply suggesting a crop, the system shows users why certain rotations may be suitable, including their potential benefits, risks, scoring, and limitations. It also provides rotation calendars and identifies information that may be missing from the available data. Other features include future climate outlooks for 2030–2049, location-specific weather forecasts, field summaries, interactive satellite layers, and an optional SerpAPI assisted chatbot feature that helps users explore information about their selected location.

Farmer Helper was developed using Python, FastAPI, and Uvicorn for the backend, and React, JavaScript, and Vite for the frontend. MapLibre GL JS powers the interactive mapping and 3D terrain visualization, while Rasterio/GDAL, NumPy, and Pillow handle geospatial data and satellite imagery. Recharts is used for data visualization, and pytest is used for backend testing. The project also uses external APIs and a geospatial dataset hosted on Hugging Face. To make the application more efficient, independent data sources are retrieved concurrently, and successful responses are cached so that previously requested information can be accessed more quickly.

What makes Farmer Helper different is the way it connects scientific data with practical farming decisions. Rather than making users search through several different platforms to understand their land, the application brings everything together in one interactive experience. It combines mapping, environmental analysis, satellite data, and crop-rotation planning into a single tool. Throughout development, we also had to consider the reliability and accuracy of different data sources, differences in geographic resolution, missing information, and the limitations of environmental models. Not every dataset represents an exact measurement of an individual field, so the application makes an effort to distinguish estimates and projections from actual observations.

Our goal with Farmer Helper is to make agricultural data more accessible and useful. As weather patterns change and farmers face increasing challenges involving soil conditions, water availability, and crop selection, having access to reliable information becomes increasingly important. We want to make it easier for farmers to understand their land, compare possible strategies, and recognize potential risks before making important decisions. Farmer Helper aims to bridge the gap between scientific research and everyday agriculture by turning publicly available data into something practical, understandable, and useful for the people who need it most.
